Group Selection: Direct vs. Social Response
metadata.display_heading: Group Selection: Direct vs. Social Response

blocks.content: As was the case for individual selection, we can decompose the response under group selection into the responses from direct and social effects, $ R_{z} = R_{d} + (n - 1) R_{s} $. Under group selection, these response components are given by [[SEE_FORMULA:22.27a]]

The covariance between the direct breeding value of a group member and the group total becomes [[SEE_FORMULA:22.27b]] Where $ \bar{r} = \sum_{j \neq i}^n r_{ij} / (n - 1) $ is the average degree of relationship (for $ i $) among group members (assuming that $ r_{ii} = 1 $, i.e., $ i $ is not inbred), resulting in $ \sum_j^n r_{ij} = 1 + (n - 1)\bar{r} $. Similarly, for the social breeding value [[SEE_FORMULA:22.27c]]

Increasing the relatedness, $r$, of group members increases the contributions from $\sigma(A_d, A_s)$ and $\sigma^2(A_s)$ by the same proportional amount, $[1+(n-1)\bar{r}]$. Hence, the relative contribution of these two components is independent of the degree of relatedness within the group. By contrast, recall that under individual selection, the relative contributions of these two components changes (and potentially can change rather dramatically) with $r$ (Equations 22.15b and 22.15c).
